title: Ethiopian Milk Pudding
community: Ethiopian dessert tradition — the set milk sweet
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Milk Pudding — whole milk thickened with cornstarch and sweetened with honey, fragrant with cardamom and rose water, set in individual cups and chilled. The Ethiopian panna cotta — smooth, barely sweet, perfumed with Ethiopian honey.
longDesc: Ethiopian milk pudding is the modern dessert restaurant classic — a set milk pudding that combines the European panna cotta format with the Ethiopian spice tradition. The cardamom and rose water make it distinctly Ethiopian while the set texture makes it elegant.
ingredients: // Topping: drizzle of honey + pinch of ground cinnamon
steps: Whisk cornstarch with ½ cup cold milk until smooth.
Heat remaining milk with honey, sugar, and cardamom until warm.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick and smooth — 8—10 minutes.
Top with a drizzle of honey and pinch of cinnamon before serving.
chefTips: Whisk the cornstarch into cold milk first — prevents lumps.
The pudding must be smooth — any lumps come from insufficient stirring.
commonMistakes: Adding cornstarch directly to hot milk — lumps.
Not stirring once it starts to thicken.
cookingScience: Cornstarch gelatinises at 62—72°C — forming a smooth gel matrix when the granules absorb water and swell. The continuous stirring during heating prevents the granules from settling and cooking unevenly, which would create lumps. The resulting gel is thermoreversible — it liquefies when reheated.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland dairy — fresh whole milk.
culturalNote: Ethiopian milk pudding is the modern Ethiopian restaurant's elegant dessert offering — using ingredients as ancient as Ethiopian honey and cardamom in the contemporary panna cotta format, it demonstrates that Ethiopian dessert culture can meet international dining expectations.
